population: YouTube-paid creators, artists, music industry intermediaries, rights holders and media companies; not individual creator earners only

reported_windows.limitations: The official artist page displays 100B as a rounded figure. Separate September 2025 official product announcement says >100B over four years. Unknown recipient counts, exact payout sum, annual split and distribution.
The CEO's January 2026 four-year statement is not a separate, additive cumulative cohort. The exact payout window is not provided in the letter.

Music-industry payouts include rights-owner intermediaries; artists may be paid indirectly. This period overlaps global creator payout windows and music payments are a subset of YouTube's payments, not additive.

rules: Neither a published rolling-four-year global payout statement nor a selected 12-month music-industry payout is a distribution of individual YouTube creator income.
The music-industry payout observation may include companies and rights holders; do not equate the recipient count to artists or the amount to take-home musician income.
One official 100B four-year window and a later official four-year statement are not independent disjoint totals and must not be added.
The July 2024 to June 2025 music payout period overlaps the other windows and cannot be added to either global sum.
Do not divide the published aggregates by channel counts, subscriber counts, video counts or surveyed creators to invent mean or median creator receipts.

The USD 100B creator/industry payout measure is not Alphabet's 2025 USD 40.367B advertising revenue, the more-than-USD 60B 2025 YouTube company revenue bound, or the separate more-than-USD 60B estimated U.S. GDP contribution.
